previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of poorly controlled type 1 diabetes, depression, and alcohol dependence was admitted for diabetic ketoacidosis after presenting with nausea, vomiting, and a glucose of 810. She had a history of recent hospitalization for DKA and NSTEMI. On admission, she was tachycardic and hypotensive but responded well to fluid resuscitation and an insulin drip. Her renal function, initially impaired with a creatinine of 2.1, improved to baseline with hydration. A mildly elevated troponin was attributed to demand ischemia rather than acute coronary occlusion. One blood culture showed coagulase-negative staphylococcus, but it was deemed contaminated, and antibiotics were stopped. Psychiatry and occupational therapy evaluated her cognitive function, noting deficits likely due to long-term diabetes and alcohol use, and recommended increased home support and family involvement. She was transitioned to a revised insulin regimen with 16 units of Lantus in the morning and 3 at dinner, plus sliding scale. She met with a diabetes educator with her daughter present. She was discharged home with home health services, a plan for follow-up in diabetes and psychiatric clinics, and continuation of all chronic medications including sertraline, aspirin, atorvastatin, and antihypertensives.
problems: Type 1 diabetes mellitus with ketoacidosis without coma
